description: The ratio column divides each status's average remaining by the mean of the status-level average remaining values, with each status weighted equally.

b.request: The ratio column is each status's average remaining (the mean of its events' per-event average `remaining`) divided by the unweighted mean of the status-level average remaining values, so each status counts equally regardless of how many events or budget lines it has
b.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.status AS status, e.event_id AS event_id, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_rem FROM event e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.status, e.event_id), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_rem) AS status_avg FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, status_avg, status_avg / (SELECT AVG(status_avg) FROM st) AS ratio FROM st

a.request: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), first work out for each event the average `remaining` and the average overspend rate, (`spent` − `amount`) ÷ `amount`, across its lines. Then, for each event `status`, average those event-level figures. Return the status, its average remaining, its average overspend rate, and its average remaining divided by the simple mean of the per-status average remaining values, with each status weighted equally. Ignore missing values in every average, and don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.status, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_remaining, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / b.amount) AS avg_overspend FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.status), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_remaining) AS avg_remaining, AVG(avg_overspend) AS avg_overspend_rate FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, avg_remaining, avg_overspend_rate, avg_remaining / (AVG(avg_remaining) OVER ()) AS remaining_ratio FROM st

c.request: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), first work out for each event the average `remaining` and the average overspend rate, (`spent` − `amount`) ÷ `amount`, across its lines. Then, for each event `status`, average those event-level figures. Show the status, its average remaining, its average overspend rate, and how its average remaining compares to the overall average remaining, as a ratio. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round anything. The ratio column divides each status's average remaining by the mean of the status-level average remaining values, with each status weighted equally.
c.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.status, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_rem, AVG(CASE WHEN b.amount IS NOT NULL AND b.amount <> 0 THEN (b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / b.amount END) AS avg_over FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.status), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_rem) AS avg_remaining, AVG(avg_over) AS avg_overspend_rate FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, avg_remaining, avg_overspend_rate, avg_remaining / (SELECT AVG(avg_remaining) FROM st) AS remaining_ratio FROM st

d.request: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), first compute for each event the average `remaining` and the average overspend rate, (`spent` − `amount`) ÷ `amount`, across its lines. Then, for each event `status`, average those event-level figures. Show each status, its average remaining, its average overspend rate, and a ratio comparing its average remaining to the overall average remaining, where the overall average remaining is the mean of the status-level average remaining values (each status weighted equally), so the ratio is the status's average remaining divided by that mean. Ignore missing values in the averages, and don't round anything.
d.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.status, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_rem, AVG(CASE WHEN b.amount IS NOT NULL AND b.amount <> 0 THEN (b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / b.amount END) AS avg_over FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.status), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_rem) AS avg_remaining, AVG(avg_over) AS avg_overspend_rate FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, avg_remaining, avg_overspend_rate, avg_remaining / (SELECT AVG(avg_remaining) FROM st) AS remaining_ratio FROM st
